output.commercial_summary: The landed cost for each supplier consists of three components: (1) the item total, calculated as unit price multiplied by the required quantity; (2) a fixed shipping charge; and (3) tax, applied at 7% of the item total (e.g., 21,375 × 0.07 = 1,496.25). Titanium Engineering Solutions provides the lowest total landed cost at $23,371.25. It is $4,931.25 cheaper than Kestrel Industrial Fasteners ($28,302.50) and $10,210.25 cheaper than Atlas Smart Robotics Corp ($33,581.50). This equates to a 17.4% cost advantage over the second‑lowest bidder and a 43.7% advantage over the highest bidder.

output.evaluation_rationale:
PRO‑SUP‑01 attained the highest overall score because it achieved perfect marks on the two most heavily weighted criteria—cost (100) and delivery (100)—and also performed strongly on risk (95), contract (90) and capability (95). The weighted aggregation therefore pushed its total to 97.5, out‑ranking the others. 

The trade‑off analysis shows that while PRO‑SUP‑02 and PRO‑SUP‑03 offer lower cost scores (82.58 and 69.6 respectively), they do not gain enough advantage in other dimensions to offset the loss. Cost savings come at the expense of higher risk or lower delivery reliability in many real‑world scenarios. In this dataset delivery is uniformly perfect (100) for all suppliers, so the differentiator becomes risk and cost. PRO‑SUP‑02 reduces cost relative to the leader but its risk score drops to 90 and its overall weighted score falls to 90.4. PRO‑SUP‑03 provides the greatest cost reduction but suffers a larger risk penalty (75) and ends with the lowest total (82.86). Thus, the model demonstrates that modest cost improvements are worthwhile only when they do not materially increase risk or erode other critical factors; otherwise the weighted score—and consequently the ranking—declines.

output.commercial_rationale: Titanium Engineering Solutions (PRO‑SUP‑01) offers the lowest landed cost at $23,371.25, delivering a 17.4% cost advantage over the next‑lowest bidder and a 43.7% advantage over the highest. The unit price ($42.75) and total landed cost are the most competitive. Delivery performance is strong with a 55‑day buffer before the required date (lead time 20 days, promised delivery 2026‑09‑21 vs required 2026‑11‑15) and a low delivery‑risk rating. The supplier’s capability – high‑precision aerospace machining – aligns directly with the technical requirements, and it holds ISO certification and a high financial‑stability score (92). All weighted evaluation criteria (cost 100, delivery 100, risk 95, contract 90, capability 95) combine to a total weighted score of 97.5, the highest among the three candidates.
